steps.question: How big are icons next to text?
steps.why: Icons match the label so they do not outweigh it.

steps.pick: neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 6.66:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.47:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Only menus and dialogs float; cards use lines.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: Subtle shadows keep the grid crisp.

steps.use: elevation.overlay and a dimmed page for dialogs
steps.why: Floating things need a shadow so they read as on top.

steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill, as in light.

steps.pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show their height as floating layers. The cast shade does this by an 8px offset and a 24px blur at 16% under the panel's edge. So a menu reads as above the grid without a heavy edge, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and shadows are subtle (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light shadow's shape for menus and dialogs in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 8px offset and 24px blur, at 50% black instead of 16%. So a menu still lifts off the dark page, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because only what floats rises (elevation.roles) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.22:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.82:1, on surface.default). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.pick: radius.4: We use a 4px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make touching panels read as separate objects, in a precise tone by brand convention. A small radius does this by breaking the outline at each corner, just softer than the 2px controls. So panels read apart yet still tile neatly, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is precise (brand.q1).

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?
steps.why: A data role keeps numbers in aligned columns.
Things that belong together sit close.

steps.pick: neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 6.66:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.47:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: How large is body text?
steps.why: Small body text fits more rows on the screen.
Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed reuses hover; experts do not need more.
Fast feedback confirms the pointer without slowing experts.
Keyboard users must always see where they are.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surface it sits on: darker in light, lighter in dark.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.

steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Small corners keep dense rows straight.
Rectangles line up in a column.

steps.rule: The edge of a control people must find.
steps.pick: neutral.500: the edge of a control people must find, 4.66:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the edge of a control people must find, 6.47:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.pick: radius.2: We use the 2px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a list row or a text area the curve of the controls beside it. So rows and fields read as one family, because the control corner is small, not a pill (shape.values), and the product is dense (content.q2).

steps.rule: A recessed fill, a step below content.
steps.pick: neutral.100, a step below content (1.13:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100, a step below content (1.25:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.

steps.pick: radius.0: We use a square corner for badges in order to give status a role of its own, apart from the 2px controls. A zero radius does this by keeping the badge a plain rectangle with no curve. So status badges line up down a table column, because badges get their own corner (shape.roles) and people scan and compare rows (tasks.q1).
neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 6.66:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.47:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
